pro-probability-prior-and-likelihood-fra.words: Resurrection probability depends jointly on its prior probability and on how strongly the historical evidence favors resurrection over the relevant competing hypotheses.
pro-probability-prior-and-likelihood-fra.critique: Strongest feature: The move supplies an explicit, logically disciplined framework connecting prior probability, evidential strength, and comparative likelihood, thereby addressing the motion at precisely the level where competing historical explanations must ultimately be evaluated. Principal limitation: It remains predominantly methodological because no numerical priors, exhaustively specified alternatives, or adequately defended likelihood assignments appear here, so the framework’s correctness cannot independently establish its desired application. Live burden: Christopoulos must demonstrate that the central burial, tomb, appearance, and witness propositions are sufficiently warranted, then show that their conjunction is substantially more expected under resurrection than under serious natural or transmission-based competitors. Locked score: The score of 90, within the very strong band, appropriately recognizes exceptional motion relevance, conceptual recoverability, careful qualification, and coherent probabilistic structure while reserving credit for the still-uncompleted empirical comparison.

pro-testimony-as-miracle-evidence.words: Testimony can provide evidence for a miracle because testimonial knowledge is generally indispensable and a sufficiently reliable report can increase a hypothesis’s probability.
pro-testimony-as-miracle-evidence.critique: Strongest feature: The move correctly resists excluding testimony categorically and advances the modest, epistemically defensible proposition that testimonial evidence can increase the probability of an event, including an alleged miracle, when relevant reliability conditions are satisfied. Principal limitation: The transition from testimony’s indispensable role in ordinary knowledge to its evidential adequacy for this extraordinary historical claim leaves provenance, independence, accuracy, distortion, and corroboration insufficiently specified, while invoking specialist consensus contributes little without their underlying reasoning. Live burden: Christopoulos must establish that the particular resurrection traditions possess confirmed access to relevant witnesses, dependable transmission, and claim-sensitive corroboration rather than relying on testimony’s general admissibility as though that settled its case-specific weight. Locked score: The score of 79, within the strong or competent band, reflects a coherent and relevant source-foundation premise whose evidential warrant remains materially conditional on qualities not demonstrated within this move.

pro-comparative-likelihood-ratio.words: The assembled evidence supports resurrection when that evidence is more expected if resurrection occurred than under the properly specified competing explanations.
pro-comparative-likelihood-ratio.critique: Strongest feature: The move articulates the correct comparative function of a likelihood ratio and directly explains why affirmative evidence and pressure against competing explanations must be assessed together rather than as disconnected collections of historical observations. Principal limitation: Disciplinary familiarity with likelihood ratios does not validate the selected evidence, guarantee exhaustive rival hypotheses, or provide defensible likelihood values, and the presentation risks sounding conclusive before those indispensable application-level inputs have been established. Live burden: Christopoulos must define the relevant evidence without dependence or inflation, specify serious heterogeneous alternatives rather than a single uniform hallucination, and justify why the entire evidential conjunction is appreciably more probable under resurrection. Locked score: The score of 86, within the very strong band, rewards excellent motion contact, conceptual coherence, and comparative orientation while appropriately discounting the absence of substantiated inputs needed to convert a sound method into a persuasive historical result.

pro-natural-regularity-miracle-context.words: A miracle is recognizable only against stable natural regularities, so ordinary experience that dead people remain dead does not conceptually exclude resurrection.
pro-natural-regularity-miracle-context.critique: Strongest feature: The move perceptively observes that a miracle conceptually presupposes stable natural regularities, because an exceptional sign would lose its recognizable contrast if comparable events occurred routinely and unpredictably throughout ordinary experience. Principal limitation: Compatibility between stable laws and an exceptional intervention does not show that observed mortality is evidentially insignificant, so the argument slides from explaining how miracles remain conceptually identifiable to minimizing the adverse prior information supplied by pervasive regularity. Live burden: Christopoulos must distinguish conceptual possibility from comparative probability and independently justify why divine intervention in this particular case offsets the exceptionally strong background frequency with which dead persons remain dead. Locked score: The score of 67, within the mixed band, appropriately credits a relevant and intelligible prior-context observation while reflecting materially overstated force, incomplete qualification, and failure to neutralize the strongest probabilistic version of the regularity objection.

tags.label: Base-rate neglect
tags.context: The move treats stable mortality as compatible with miracles but insufficiently preserves its substantial adverse significance for the resurrection prior.

pro-incarnation-context-and-resurrection.words: If God might fittingly become incarnate and authenticate that mission through resurrection, Jesus’s resurrection need not begin with an evidentially prohibitive prior.
pro-incarnation-context-and-resurrection.critique: Strongest feature: The move carefully frames its conclusion conditionally and proportionately, arguing only that resurrection’s prior need not be insurmountably low if divine existence, incarnation, atonement, moral instruction, and miraculous authentication receive appreciable background probability. Principal limitation: Possibility of God does not itself determine the probability of incarnation or resurrection, while descriptions of divine purposes as fitting or modestly likely remain broad judgments unsupported by an independent account of perfect divine action. Live burden: Christopoulos must warrant each conditional transition from God’s existence to incarnation and from incarnation to resurrection as authentication, while comparing those proposed purposes with alternative divine choices and the evidential obscurity emphasized by Dillahunty. Locked score: The score of 77, within the strong or competent band, recognizes coherent conditional reasoning, explicit uncertainty, and useful prior context while discounting underdeveloped divine-purpose likelihoods and limited completion of the motion-level comparison.

pro-new-testament-reliability-foundation.words: Internal historical texture, authorship traditions, firsthand narrative indicators, external confirmations, and regionally accurate names jointly support reliable access to early resurrection testimony.
pro-new-testament-reliability-foundation.critique: Strongest feature: The move offers a cumulative and directly relevant source foundation, identifying several potentially convergent indicators including historical texture, traditional authorship, firsthand narrative characteristics, external confirmation, and geographically appropriate naming patterns rather than resting everything on one consideration. Principal limitation: Reliability, eyewitness access, and external confirmation are applied too globally across distinct documents, while representative examples, source dependence, authorship disputes, transmission pathways, and the precise historical propositions independently corroborated remain insufficiently differentiated. Live burden: Christopoulos must evaluate each document and tradition separately, establish which sources are genuinely independent and proximal, and demonstrate that corroborated incidental details meaningfully transfer credibility to the central death, burial, tomb, and appearance claims. Locked score: The score of 80, within the strong or competent band, reflects substantial relevance and a promising cumulative structure while preserving significant deductions for broad terminology, implicit qualifications, and underdeveloped document-specific verification.

pro-known-burial-and-empty-tomb.words: A known burial, failure to produce Jesus’s body, multiple attestations, hostile acknowledgment, and discovery by women collectively support an authentic empty tomb.
pro-known-burial-and-empty-tomb.critique: Strongest feature: The move assembles several mutually relevant considerations for a known burial and authentic empty tomb, including public location, nonproduction of a body, multiple narrative lines, purported hostile acknowledgment, and the potentially counterproductive placement of women as initial discoverers. Principal limitation: The evidential force depends heavily on source independence and historical context, because shared traditions can generate multiple narratives, silence about producing a body is not independent confirmation, and the women-witness criterion requires careful cultural and literary qualification. Live burden: Christopoulos must first establish Jesus’s death, actual placement in an identifiable tomb, and the reliability and independence of the relevant attestations before treating subsequent emptiness as fixed data demanding explanation. Locked score: The score of 78, within the strong or competent band, credits direct engagement with central historical data while discounting overstated cumulative force, undifferentiated attestations, and incomplete treatment of stronger transmission-based alternatives.

pro-diverse-multimodal-appearances.words: Numerous witnesses reportedly experienced diverse, detailed, multimodal encounters across many occasions, placing substantial pressure on collusion and uniform shared-hallucination explanations.
pro-diverse-multimodal-appearances.critique: Strongest feature: The move emphasizes the breadth, duration, physical detail, and reported multimodality of the appearance traditions, thereby identifying a conjunction that would indeed be difficult to explain through deliberate collusion or one simultaneous identical hallucination. Principal limitation: It treats a uniform shared hallucination as the principal natural competitor without establishing the reports’ independence, firsthand provenance, or descriptive accuracy, and it insufficiently considers heterogeneous experiences, memory development, mistaken identification, and later narrative harmonization. Live burden: Christopoulos must verify which named witnesses support which experiential details, separate independent testimony from inherited tradition, and compare resurrection against mixed natural and transmission-based explanations rather than requiring every report to arise through a single psychological mechanism. Locked score: The score of 72, within the mixed band, rewards direct relevance and ambitious explanatory comparison while reflecting materially overstated warrant, unstable scope, missing qualifications, and an inadequately charitable rival model.

tags.label: Scope neglect
tags.context: The comparison concentrates on one uniform shared hallucination while underexamining a broader collection of heterogeneous natural and transmission-based explanations.

pro-conversion-and-costly-witness-conduc.words: Paul’s conversion and costly witness conduct support sincere resurrection belief and weigh against deliberate fabrication, though sincerity alone cannot establish historical truth.
pro-conversion-and-costly-witness-conduc.critique: Strongest feature: The move plausibly uses Paul’s reversal and costly commitment to challenge an uncomplicated deception hypothesis, since hostility, suffering, and sustained adherence can provide meaningful evidence that at least some proponents sincerely accepted resurrection-related experiences. Principal limitation: The claimed identities, firsthand opportunities, and specific circumstances of suffering or death remain broadly scoped, while sincere commitment cannot distinguish accurate perception and transmission from honest mistake, memory development, or inherited conviction. Live burden: Christopoulos must identify which witnesses knowingly faced avoidable costs for claims grounded in their own experiences, document those costs, and integrate sincerity with independently reliable appearance evidence rather than allowing commitment to substitute for factual verification. Locked score: The score of 74, within the mixed band, credits a reasonable sincerity inference and relevant pressure against fabrication while discounting overextension toward truth, insufficient witness-specific support, and incomplete engagement with sincere-error alternatives.

con-source-account-disparities.words: Unresolved differences among the resurrection narratives reduce their reliability, particularly when those accounts are presented as divinely inspired evidence for a uniquely important event.
con-source-account-disparities.critique: Strongest feature: The reply directly contacts the affirmative source foundation by identifying concrete categories of narrative variation involving visitors, guards, timing, purpose, the stone, and an earthquake, thereby challenging undifferentiated claims of historical reliability. Principal limitation: It does not establish which disparities are genuinely contradictory, central, or resistant to reasonable reconciliation, and tying their seriousness to divine inspiration risks targeting a theological property that the historical case need not require. Live burden: Dillahunty must distinguish ordinary perspectival variation from discrepancies that materially reduce confidence in burial, emptiness, or appearances, then explain why those specific differences outweigh shared content or any independently supported details. Locked score: The score of 79, within the strong or competent band, appropriately recognizes a responsive and relevant reliability challenge while preserving deductions for collective treatment of disparities, incomplete source-by-source analysis, and only partial engagement with the affirmative’s cumulative confirmations.

con-source-corroboration-deficit.words: The resurrection case lacks confirmed primary witnesses, contemporary corroboration, hostile attestation, and reproducible investigation sufficient to support its extraordinary historical conclusion.
con-source-corroboration-deficit.critique: Strongest feature: The reply forcefully targets decisive provenance and corroboration requirements, distinguishing claimed eyewitness access from confirmed primary testimony and emphasizing the limited capacity for independent historical investigation of the resurrection narratives. Principal limitation: Categorical language about having no empirical evidence, contemporary account, or corroboration outruns the demonstrated survey and risks collapsing disputed indirect evidence into literal absence, even though later testimony and internal indicators can possess limited historical value. Live burden: Dillahunty must define the evidential standard appropriate to ancient singular events, evaluate the affirmative’s proposed sources and confirmations individually, and show why their cumulative weight remains inadequate without presupposing that only contemporaneous or directly reproducible evidence can count. Locked score: The score of 79, within the strong or competent band, rewards exceptional responsiveness and central relevance while reflecting overstatement, insufficient representative source analysis, and reduced charity toward the affirmative’s acknowledged indirect evidential categories.

con-death-confirmation-required.words: Before resurrection can be inferred, Jesus’s actual death must be historically established through evidence adequate to exclude mistaken determination or premature burial.
con-death-confirmation-required.critique: Strongest feature: The reply identifies an indispensable logical prerequisite with unusual clarity: unless Jesus actually died, no subsequent recovery or disappearance can constitute resurrection, so evidential scrutiny must begin before burial and tomb interpretation. Principal limitation: Describing the available narrative as propaganda from a biased source prejudges its reliability and leaves the required degree of independent confirmation unspecified, potentially suggesting a modern forensic standard unavailable for most ancient deaths. Live burden: Dillahunty must show why the relevant narrative, contextual, and medical considerations fail collectively to establish death to an appropriate historical confidence, while distinguishing reasonable demands for convergence from unattainable contemporary certification. Locked score: The score of 85, within the very strong band, recognizes a coherent, precise, highly responsive necessary-condition challenge while retaining deductions for rhetorically loaded source characterization, incomplete assessment of convergent indicators, and ambiguity about the appropriate confirmation threshold.

con-sincerity-transmission-limits.words: Witness sincerity cannot ensure factual accuracy because honest people may be mistaken, and later transmission can distort even an initially sincere statement.
con-sincerity-transmission-limits.critique: Strongest feature: The reply precisely separates three questions that the affirmative risks blending: whether a witness speaks honestly, whether the underlying experience was accurately interpreted, and whether the resulting statement was transmitted without later alteration or embellishment. Principal limitation: Establishing that mistake and distortion are possible does not demonstrate their occurrence or magnitude in these traditions, and the affirmative principally uses costly conduct against deliberate deception rather than treating sincerity alone as conclusive proof. Live burden: Dillahunty must connect the general possibilities of sincere error and transmission distortion to particular witnesses, sources, or narrative developments while showing that the affirmative’s additional appearance evidence cannot adequately compensate for those vulnerabilities. Locked score: The score of 91, within the very strong band, reflects excellent conceptual precision, calibration, charity, responsiveness, and central relevance while reserving limited credit because the move diagnoses pathways of error without independently establishing their historical realization.

con-empty-tomb-unconfirmed.words: No resurrection explanation is required until an identifiable tomb, Jesus’s placement within it, and his subsequent absence are established as reliable historical data.
con-empty-tomb-unconfirmed.critique: Strongest feature: The reply delivers a sharp diagnostic challenge by identifying the exact evidential sequence required before explanatory comparison begins: a real tomb must be identified, Jesus must have occupied it, and his body must subsequently have been absent. Principal limitation: Its dismissive characterization of the tomb as merely a hole in the ground understates the affirmative’s cumulative considerations and does not itself assess the alleged known location, multiple attestations, hostile response, or women-discovery tradition. Live burden: Dillahunty must demonstrate why those proposed indicators lack sufficient reliability or independence, while preserving the appropriately conditional conclusion that no resurrection explanation is owed unless the foundational tomb propositions become established. Locked score: The score of 89, within the very strong band, rewards exceptional precision, responsiveness, calibration, and burden diagnosis while reflecting the limited evidential development supporting the claim that the affirmative’s offered foundations remain unconfirmed.

con-conditional-probability-direction.words: Expected resurrection reports given resurrection must not be confused with a high probability of resurrection given the existence of those reports.
con-conditional-probability-direction.critique: Strongest feature: The reply states an indispensable probabilistic distinction with exceptional clarity, separating the probability of reports given resurrection from the posterior probability of resurrection given reports and illustrating the error through an accessible alien-abduction comparison. Principal limitation: Christopoulos explicitly invoked priors and comparative likelihood ratios, so the reply identifies a serious inferential danger without conclusively showing that the affirmative actually reversed the conditional or relied upon the resurrection likelihood alone. Live burden: Dillahunty must demonstrate where the affirmative’s application omits priors, rival likelihoods, dependence corrections, or normalization, thereby converting a valid diagnostic warning into a source-specific defeat of the comparative case. Locked score: The score of 94, within the very strong band, appropriately reflects outstanding logical coherence, precision, motion relevance, and direct responsiveness while retaining the narrow qualification that identifying a possible inverse-probability error is not identical to proving its commission.

con-costly-commitment-not-truth.words: Willingness to endure persecution or death can support sincerity and commitment, but neither property makes the underlying resurrection belief historically true.
con-costly-commitment-not-truth.critique: Strongest feature: The reply grants the strongest legitimate affirmative conclusion that costly conduct can indicate sincerity, then precisely explains why conviction, sacrifice, popularity, or numerical commitment cannot themselves determine whether the underlying resurrection proposition is true. Principal limitation: The affirmative uses suffering primarily to disfavor conscious fabrication and to support sincerely reported experience, so the reply would overreach if interpreted as showing that costly behavior has no evidential relevance whatsoever. Live burden: Dillahunty must preserve the concession that commitment can update against deliberate deception while demonstrating that it neither confirms firsthand status nor discriminates accurate resurrection perception from sincere mistake, memory alteration, or transmitted belief. Locked score: The score of 94, within the very strong band, rewards exceptional coherence, evidential warrant, charity, responsiveness, and inferential precision while recognizing that the move defeats a truth inference rather than eliminating every narrower evidential use of costly commitment.

con-divine-action-expectations.words: Incarnation’s alleged fittingness does not by itself raise resurrection probability, and the proposed divine strategy leaves obscure testimony and sacrificial suffering insufficiently explained.
con-divine-action-expectations.critique: Strongest feature: The reply properly demands a resurrection-specific inferential bridge, observing that even a justified claim about God choosing ideal action or human incarnation would not automatically determine the probability of resurrection as the chosen method of authentication. Principal limitation: Its categorical dismissal overlooks Christopoulos’s explicit proposal that resurrection fittingly validates incarnation, while Dillahunty’s competing expectations about perfect divine disclosure, obscurity, and sacrificial means remain asserted more than independently defended. Live burden: Dillahunty must compare the proposed authentication rationale with plausible alternative divine actions and explain why a perfectly acting God would be unlikely to select resurrection under the stipulated purposes, rather than merely noting that incarnation alone is insufficient. Locked score: The score of 76, within the strong or competent band, credits relevant contact and a sound demand for an additional conditional bridge while reflecting incomplete engagement, underdeveloped divine expectations, and only moderate logical execution.

con-alternatives-burden-preserved.words: Defeating one natural explanation does not establish resurrection; the affirmative must still warrant its historical data, priors, and comparative likelihoods.
con-alternatives-burden-preserved.critique: Strongest feature: The reply correctly preserves the affirmative burden and explains that failure to establish a selected naturalistic alternative does not automatically validate resurrection, especially when the reliability of the underlying biblical accounts remains independently disputed. Principal limitation: The courtroom analogy can obscure that a genuinely exhaustive probabilistic comparison may rationally favor one hypothesis without deductively disproving every competitor, so the point succeeds only against elimination-based reasoning or poorly grounded likelihood assignments. Live burden: Dillahunty must show that the affirmative’s hypothesis set is incomplete, its evidence insufficiently warranted, or its comparative likelihoods unsupported rather than treating rational suspension as an automatic consequence of every unresolved alternative. Locked score: The score of 93, within the very strong band, reflects exceptional responsiveness, motion relevance, calibration, and burden discipline while preserving the important qualification that comparative support does not require conclusive refutation of each rival hypothesis.

con-rational-uncertainty-option.words: An exhaustive hypothesis set does not require belief in its largest member when probability assignments remain poorly grounded or every option lacks sufficient evidential support.
con-rational-uncertainty-option.critique: Strongest feature: The reply clearly distinguishes logical exhaustiveness, relative probabilistic ranking, and sufficient warrant for belief, preserving the rational option of saying the event remains unknown when the available data cannot support dependable assignments. Principal limitation: The reference to one-half may be too restrictive for every epistemic or decision context, because a hypothesis can be the rationally preferred member of a multi-option distribution without exceeding that threshold, even if outright belief remains unwarranted. Live burden: Dillahunty must connect rational suspension to deficiencies in this case’s priors, source reliability, dependence structure, and rival likelihoods rather than relying solely on the abstract possibility that no hypothesis receives sufficient support. Locked score: The score of 94, within the very strong band, rewards outstanding motion contact, precision, coherent calibration, and a proportionate uncertainty-preserving conclusion while acknowledging distinctions among ranking, action, confidence, and belief.
